translations.title: US To Mexico Logistics: The Complete Guide For Shippers In 2026
translations.excerpt: Moving goods from the United States into Mexico is not domestic trucking with an extra stop. It is an export from one country and an import into another, and the import side is where most shipments fail. This guide walks the entire lane end to end.
translations.content:
US to Mexico logistics means moving freight from a US origin, across a land border crossing such as Laredo, through Mexican customs clearance, and on to a final Mexican destination. Every shipment needs a Mexican importer of record, a licensed Mexican customs broker, a pedimento, and correct HS classification. Typical door-to-door transit is 3 to 5 business days from Texas to central Mexico when documents are clean; documentation problems, not distance, cause most delays.

  • Port Laredo handled 353.94 billion dollars of trade in 2025, up 4.4 percent over 2024, with more than 97 percent of it tied to Mexico. It remains the top US land port.
  • Mexican law requires a licensed customs broker (agente aduanal) for virtually all commercial imports. A US freight forwarder alone cannot clear your goods.
  • The importer of record must be a Mexican tax-registered entity with an RFC and must appear on the padrón de importadores. Foreign sellers without a Mexican entity need a FIOR or an import-of-record service.
  • From 1 August 2026 the Manifestación de Valor must be filed electronically through VUTCE. The paper transition ended 31 July 2026.
  • Mexico's standard IVA is 16 percent and is calculated on the customs value plus duty, not on the invoice value alone.

What does US to Mexico logistics actually involve?

An export clearance on the US side, a border crossing, a Mexican import clearance with a pedimento, and domestic delivery inside Mexico. Four distinct stages, each with its own paperwork.

The single most expensive misconception in this lane is treating Mexico as an extension of domestic US trucking. It is not. A shipment from Dallas to Monterrey is roughly the same distance as Dallas to Denver, but the two moves have almost nothing in common operationally. A US to Mexico shipment passes through four stages. First, US export clearance, which for most commercial goods means an Electronic Export Information filing when the shipment value exceeds the reporting threshold. Second, the physical border crossing, where a drayage carrier moves the trailer across the bridge. Third, Mexican import clearance, where a licensed Mexican customs broker files a pedimento and pays duties and IVA on behalf of the importer of record. Fourth, domestic delivery from the border to the final destination. Most shippers plan carefully for stages one, two and four, then discover that stage three is where everything actually stops. Mexican customs is documentary. It does not care how good your carrier is if the classification is wrong or the value manifest is missing. The practical consequence is that your choice of Mexican customs broker matters more than your choice of trucking company. A good broker prevents delays. A trucking company can only wait through them.

Who can legally import into Mexico?

Only a Mexican tax-registered entity holding an RFC and listed on the padrón de importadores. Foreign companies cannot import into Mexico in their own name.

This is the requirement that stops most US and international sellers, and it is worth stating plainly: you cannot import into Mexico as a foreign company. The importer of record must be a Mexican entity with an RFC (Registro Federal de Contribuyentes) and must be enrolled in the padrón de importadores, the official importer registry. Certain regulated categories additionally require enrolment in a sector-specific padrón. There are three workable structures. You can establish a Mexican legal entity, which gives you full control but takes months and creates ongoing tax obligations. You can sell on DDP terms to a Mexican buyer who imports in their own name, which is simplest but means you lose control of the customs process and your buyer absorbs the compliance burden. Or you can use a Foreign Importer of Record service, where a Mexican entity acts as importer on your behalf. The third route is what most Amazon Mexico and e-commerce sellers use, and it is what Amazon itself expects when it asks a foreign seller for a FIOR. It is legitimate and widely used, but it is a real legal relationship with real liability, not a paperwork formality. The FIOR is answerable to Mexican customs for the accuracy of what is declared. Whichever route you take, decide it before you ship, not while your trailer is parked in Nuevo Laredo.

How long does freight take from the US to Mexico?

Three to five business days door to door from Texas to central Mexico with clean documents. Border dwell time, not driving time, is the main variable.

Driving time is the predictable part. Laredo to Monterrey is roughly 230 kilometres and takes a few hours. Laredo to Mexico City is around 1,100 kilometres and is a long day and a half of driving. Neither of those numbers is what determines your delivery date. What determines it is border dwell. A shipment with a complete document set, correct classification and a broker who has the pedimento prepared in advance can cross and clear in under a day. A shipment missing a permit, carrying a value that customs questions, or classified under a code that triggers a regulatory requirement can sit for a week or longer. Mexican customs also applies a randomised inspection mechanism at clearance, so a proportion of shipments are physically examined regardless of how clean the paperwork is. You cannot avoid this, but you can make it fast: goods that match their description and documentation clear examination quickly. A realistic planning assumption for a well-documented LTL or FTL shipment is three to five business days from a Texas warehouse to a central Mexican destination. Build a buffer beyond that for first shipments, regulated categories, and anything crossing during peak season.

What does it cost to ship from the US to Mexico?

Freight, customs brokerage, duty, IVA and any inspection or storage charges. IVA at 16 percent applied to customs value plus duty is usually the largest single line.

Cross-border quotes are frequently compared wrongly because different providers include different things. Break the cost into components and compare like with like. Freight is the transport itself, which may be a single through-carrier or a combination of US linehaul, drayage across the bridge, and a Mexican domestic carrier. Customs brokerage is the fee charged by the Mexican agente aduanal for preparing and filing the pedimento; this is a professional fee and is separate from the taxes. Duty depends entirely on HS classification and origin. IVA is 16 percent, applied to the customs value plus duty, which means duty compounds into the tax base. Then there are the charges that do not appear on any quote: inspection fees if your shipment is selected for examination, storage if it is held, demurrage if a trailer waits, and correction costs if a pedimento has to be amended. These are the items that turn a competitive quote into an expensive shipment. One structural point worth understanding: goods that qualify under USMCA rules of origin and are supported by a valid certificate of origin can enter duty free. Goods that merely ship from the United States do not qualify. Origin is about where the goods were produced or substantially transformed, not where they were loaded. Turkish, Chinese or European goods warehoused in Texas remain Turkish, Chinese or European for customs purposes.

What documents does a US to Mexico shipment need?

Commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, pedimento, electronic Manifestación de Valor, and a USMCA certificate of origin where the goods qualify.

The commercial invoice must show a defensible transaction value, a clear description of the goods, and the parties. Vague descriptions such as 'samples', 'parts' or 'gifts' invite questioning and delay. The pedimento is the Mexican customs declaration itself, prepared and filed by your customs broker. It is the definitive legal record of the import and is what you will be asked for in any later audit. The Manifestación de Valor is a sworn statement supporting the declared customs value. This is the document with an immediate deadline: following the extension published on 2 June 2026, the coexistence period for the paper format ended on 31 July 2026, and from 1 August 2026 electronic filing through VUTCE is mandatory. Anyone still relying on the paper format needs to have moved. A USMCA certificate of origin is required to claim preferential duty treatment, and only for goods that genuinely qualify. Claiming preference on non-qualifying goods is a compliance exposure, not a shortcut. Regulated categories add their own layer. Food, supplements, cosmetics and medical devices may require COFEPRIS authorisation; electronics and appliances may require NOM certification and Spanish-language labelling. These are determined by HS code, which is why classification is the first thing to get right rather than the last.

Three ways to structure a US to Mexico import

StructureHow it worksBest suited to
Own Mexican entityYou register a Mexican company, obtain an RFC and enrol in the padrón de importadoresEstablished volume, long-term market commitment
Sell DDP to a Mexican buyerYour customer imports in their own name and handles clearanceB2B sales to importers who already have the structure
Foreign Importer of Record (FIOR)A Mexican entity acts as importer of record on your behalfE-commerce and Amazon Mexico sellers without a local entity

Definitions

  • Pedimento: The pedimento is the official Mexican customs declaration filed for every import and export, and it is the legal record of what was declared, classified and paid.
  • Agente aduanal: An agente aduanal is a licensed Mexican customs broker who is legally authorised to file customs declarations and who carries personal liability for their accuracy.
  • Padrón de importadores: The padrón de importadores is Mexico's official register of authorised importers, and an entity must be listed on it before it can import commercially.

Frequently asked questions

Can a US company import into Mexico in its own name?

No. The importer of record must be a Mexican tax-registered entity with an RFC and enrolment in the padrón de importadores. A US company must either establish a Mexican entity, sell DDP to a Mexican importer, or use a Foreign Importer of Record service.

Do I need a Mexican customs broker?

For virtually all commercial imports, yes. Mexican law requires a licensed agente aduanal to file the pedimento. A US freight forwarder can arrange transport but cannot clear goods through Mexican customs.

How long does it take to ship from Texas to Mexico?

Three to five business days door to door to central Mexico with complete documents. Border dwell time is the main variable, not driving distance. Documentation problems can extend this to a week or more.

Are goods shipped from the US duty free under USMCA?

Only if the goods themselves qualify under USMCA rules of origin and are supported by a valid certificate of origin. Shipping from the United States does not by itself confer origin. Goods produced elsewhere and warehoused in the US do not qualify.

What is the IVA on imports into Mexico?

The standard IVA rate is 16 percent, calculated on the customs value plus any applicable duty rather than on the invoice value alone. This means duty increases the tax base.

What changed on 1 August 2026?

Electronic filing of the Manifestación de Valor through VUTCE became mandatory. The coexistence period allowing the paper format ended on 31 July 2026, following the extension published by SAT on 2 June 2026.

translations.title: Logística De Estados Unidos A México: Guía Completa Para Importadores 2026
translations.excerpt: Importar desde Estados Unidos no es transporte con una parada extra. Es una exportación y una importación, y la parte mexicana es donde se detienen la mayoría de los embarques. Esta guía recorre el proceso completo desde la perspectiva del importador mexicano.
translations.content:
La logística de Estados Unidos a México consiste en mover mercancía desde origen estadounidense, cruzar una aduana terrestre como Nuevo Laredo, despachar la importación ante la aduana mexicana mediante pedimento, y entregar en destino nacional. Se requiere estar inscrito en el padrón de importadores, contar con RFC y trabajar con un agente aduanal. El tránsito realista de Texas al centro del país es de 3 a 5 días hábiles con documentación completa.

  • El puerto de Laredo movió 353.94 mil millones de dólares en 2025, un aumento de 4.4 por ciento respecto a 2024, y más del 97 por ciento de ese comercio está vinculado a México.
  • Desde el 1 de agosto de 2026 la Manifestación de Valor debe presentarse electrónicamente por VUTCE. El periodo de coexistencia con el formato impreso terminó el 31 de julio de 2026.
  • El IVA general de importación es 16 por ciento y se calcula sobre el valor en aduana más el impuesto general de importación, no sólo sobre el valor de factura.
  • El importador debe estar inscrito en el padrón de importadores; ciertas mercancías requieren además inscripción en un padrón sectorial.
  • La Ley Federal de Protección al Consumidor establece en su artículo 77 que la garantía no puede ser inferior a sesenta días contados a partir de la entrega del bien.

¿Qué implica realmente importar desde Estados Unidos?

Cuatro etapas: despacho de exportación en Estados Unidos, cruce fronterizo, despacho de importación en México con pedimento, y distribución nacional.

Muchos importadores mexicanos que empiezan a comprar en Estados Unidos calculan el costo como si fuera flete nacional más un cruce. El resultado es un presupuesto que se rompe en la primera operación. La operación tiene cuatro etapas claramente separadas. En la primera, el exportador estadounidense presenta su declaración de exportación cuando el valor lo requiere. En la segunda, un transportista de cruce lleva la caja por el puente internacional. En la tercera, su agente aduanal presenta el pedimento ante la aduana mexicana y determina las contribuciones. En la cuarta, un transportista nacional entrega en destino. La etapa tres es donde se concentran los problemas y también donde usted tiene más control del que cree. La aduana mexicana es documental: la clasificación arancelaria, el valor declarado y los permisos determinan si su embarque cruza en horas o se queda una semana. Por eso la decisión más importante que tomará no es qué transportista contrata, sino con qué agente aduanal trabaja y con cuánta anticipación le entrega la documentación.

¿Qué necesito para importar legalmente a México?

RFC vigente, inscripción en el padrón de importadores, agente aduanal, y en su caso inscripción en padrón sectorial y permisos regulatorios.

El primer requisito es fiscal: una persona física con actividad empresarial o una persona moral con RFC activo. Sin RFC no hay padrón, y sin padrón no hay importación comercial. El segundo es la inscripción en el padrón de importadores ante el SAT. El trámite requiere e.firma vigente, domicilio fiscal localizado y opinión de cumplimiento positiva. Es aquí donde se caen muchas solicitudes: si su opinión de cumplimiento está en negativo por un adeudo o una declaración omitida, el padrón no procede hasta regularizarlo. El tercero es el padrón sectorial cuando la mercancía lo exige. Calzado, textiles, productos siderúrgicos, químicos y otros sectores tienen registro específico adicional. Se determina por fracción arancelaria, no por el nombre comercial del producto. El cuarto son los permisos y regulaciones no arancelarias: COFEPRIS para alimentos, suplementos, cosméticos y dispositivos médicos; NOM y etiquetado en español para múltiples categorías de consumo. Conviene resolver esto antes de comprar, no cuando la mercancía ya está en la frontera. Un punto que ahorra dinero: la inscripción al padrón puede tardar semanas. Inicie el trámite mientras negocia con su proveedor, no después.

¿Cuánto cuesta importar desde Estados Unidos?

Flete, honorarios del agente aduanal, impuesto general de importación, IVA del 16 por ciento, DTA y gastos de maniobra o almacenaje.

El error más común al comparar cotizaciones es no separar los conceptos. Un proveedor que cotiza barato el flete puede estar dejando fuera honorarios, maniobras y previos que otro sí incluye. El flete puede ser un servicio integrado o la suma de linehaul estadounidense, cruce y transporte nacional. Los honorarios del agente aduanal son la contraprestación profesional por el despacho y son independientes de las contribuciones. El impuesto general de importación depende de la fracción arancelaria y del origen. El IVA es 16 por ciento sobre el valor en aduana más el impuesto general de importación, de modo que el arancel aumenta la base gravable. El DTA es el derecho de trámite aduanero. Después vienen los cargos que no aparecen en ninguna cotización: reconocimiento aduanero si le toca, almacenaje si la mercancía se queda, y rectificaciones de pedimento si algo se declaró mal. Estos conceptos son los que convierten una importación barata en cara. Sobre el T-MEC conviene ser preciso. La mercancía originaria de Estados Unidos, Canadá o México que cumple las reglas de origen y cuenta con certificación válida puede entrar libre de arancel. Mercancía china, europea o asiática que simplemente se almacenó en Texas no es originaria y paga el arancel que le corresponda. El origen se determina por donde se produjo o transformó sustancialmente la mercancía, no por dónde se cargó el camión.

¿Cuánto tarda un embarque de Estados Unidos a México?

De 3 a 5 días hábiles de Texas al centro del país con documentación completa. El tiempo en frontera, no la distancia, es la variable principal.

Las distancias son cortas y predecibles. De Laredo a Monterrey son alrededor de 230 kilómetros. De Laredo a la Ciudad de México, alrededor de 1,100 kilómetros. Ninguna de esas cifras determina su fecha de entrega. Lo que la determina es el despacho. Un embarque con pedimento preparado con anticipación, clasificación correcta y valor sustentado cruza y despacha en menos de un día. Un embarque al que le falta un permiso, cuyo valor la autoridad cuestiona, o cuya fracción arancelaria activa una regulación no prevista, puede quedarse una semana o más. Existe además el mecanismo de selección automatizada, por lo que una proporción de los embarques recibe reconocimiento aduanero independientemente de qué tan limpia esté la documentación. No se puede evitar, pero sí se puede hacer rápido: mercancía que coincide con lo declarado se libera pronto. Para planeación, considere de 3 a 5 días hábiles puerta a puerta al centro del país con documentación en orden, y agregue holgura para primeras operaciones, mercancía regulada y temporada alta.

¿Qué documentos se necesitan?

Factura comercial, lista de empaque, carta porte, pedimento, Manifestación de Valor electrónica y certificación de origen T-MEC cuando aplique.

La factura comercial debe reflejar un valor de transacción sustentable y una descripción precisa. Descripciones genéricas como 'muestras' o 'refacciones' invitan al cuestionamiento del valor. El pedimento es la declaración aduanera y el documento legal definitivo de la operación. Consérvelo: es lo que le van a pedir en cualquier revisión posterior. La Manifestación de Valor es la declaración bajo protesta que sustenta el valor en aduana, y es el punto con fecha límite inmediata. Tras la prórroga publicada por el SAT el 2 de junio de 2026, que reformó el artículo Décimo Primero Transitorio de las RGCE 2026, el periodo de coexistencia con el formato impreso concluyó el 31 de julio de 2026. Desde el 1 de agosto de 2026 la presentación electrónica por VUTCE es obligatoria. La certificación de origen T-MEC sólo aplica a mercancía que efectivamente califica. Declarar preferencia sobre mercancía no originaria es una contingencia, no un ahorro. Y cuando venda al consumidor final en México, recuerde el marco de PROFECO: el artículo 77 de la Ley Federal de Protección al Consumidor establece que la garantía no puede ser inferior a sesenta días desde la entrega, y el artículo 92 TER fija la bonificación mínima en veinte por ciento del precio pagado cuando procede.

Conceptos de costo en una importación desde Estados Unidos

FleteTransporte de origen a destinoDistancia, modalidad LTL o FTL, temporada
Honorarios de agente aduanalServicio profesional de despachoComplejidad de la operación y número de fracciones
Impuesto general de importaciónArancelFracción arancelaria y origen de la mercancía
IVA16 por cientoValor en aduana más impuesto general de importación

Definiciones

  • Padrón de importadores: El padrón de importadores es el registro del SAT en el que debe estar inscrita toda persona que realice importaciones comerciales a México.
  • Manifestación de Valor: La Manifestación de Valor es la declaración bajo protesta de decir verdad con los elementos que sustentan el valor en aduana de la mercancía importada.
  • Reconocimiento aduanero: El reconocimiento aduanero es la revisión física y documental que practica la autoridad cuando el mecanismo de selección automatizada así lo determina.

Preguntas frecuentes

¿Necesito estar en el padrón de importadores para importar de Estados Unidos?

Sí. Toda importación comercial requiere que el importador esté inscrito en el padrón de importadores ante el SAT, con RFC activo, e.firma vigente y opinión de cumplimiento positiva. Ciertas mercancías exigen además padrón sectorial.

¿Puedo importar sin agente aduanal?

En la práctica no para operaciones comerciales. El despacho aduanero se realiza mediante agente aduanal o agencia aduanal autorizada, que presenta el pedimento y responde por su contenido.

¿Toda la mercancía que viene de Estados Unidos entra libre de arancel por el T-MEC?

No. Sólo la mercancía originaria conforme a las reglas de origen del T-MEC y con certificación válida. Mercancía producida en China, Europa o Asia que únicamente se almacenó en Estados Unidos no es originaria y paga arancel.

¿Sobre qué base se calcula el IVA de importación?

Sobre el valor en aduana más el impuesto general de importación y, en su caso, otras contribuciones. No se calcula únicamente sobre el valor de la factura, por lo que el arancel incrementa la base del IVA.

¿Qué cambió el 1 de agosto de 2026?

La presentación electrónica de la Manifestación de Valor por VUTCE se volvió obligatoria. El periodo de coexistencia con el formato impreso terminó el 31 de julio de 2026, conforme a la prórroga publicada por el SAT el 2 de junio de 2026.

¿Cuál es la garantía mínima que debo dar al consumidor en México?

El artículo 77 de la Ley Federal de Protección al Consumidor establece que la garantía no puede ser inferior a sesenta días contados a partir de la entrega del bien o la prestación total del servicio.

translations.title: ABD'den Meksika'ya Lojistik: Türk Satıcılar İçin Tam Rehber 2026
translations.excerpt: Türkiye'den Meksika'ya satış yapanların çoğu ABD üzerinden geçiyor ama USMCA muafiyetinin kendilerini kapsamadığını gümrükte öğreniyor. Bu rehber rotanın tamamını, Türk satıcının gerçek kısıtlarıyla birlikte anlatıyor.
translations.content:
ABD'den Meksika'ya lojistik, malın ABD'deki bir depodan Laredo gibi bir kara sınır kapısından geçirilip Meksika gümrüğünde pedimento ile beyan edilmesi ve iç dağıtımla teslim edilmesidir. Meksika'ya ticari ithalat için RFC sahibi bir Meksika tüzel kişiliği, ithalatçı siciline kayıt ve lisanslı gümrük müşaviri zorunludur. Türk menşeli ürünler USMCA muafiyetinden yararlanamaz; ABD'de depolanmış olmaları menşei değiştirmez.

  • Laredo limanı 2025'te 353,94 milyar dolarlık ticaret hacmine ulaştı, bir önceki yıla göre yüzde 4,4 artışla, ve bu hacmin yüzde 97'den fazlası Meksika bağlantılı.
  • Türkiye USMCA üyesi değildir. Türk menşeli ürün ABD deposunda beklese bile Meksika gümrüğünde Türk menşeli sayılır ve tercihli tarifeden yararlanamaz.
  • 1 Ağustos 2026'dan itibaren Değer Beyanı'nın VUTCE üzerinden elektronik verilmesi zorunlu hale geldi; kağıt format için birlikte var olma süresi 31 Temmuz 2026'da sona erdi.
  • Meksika'da standart IVA oranı yüzde 16'dır ve fatura değeri üzerinden değil, gümrük değeri artı vergi üzerinden hesaplanır.
  • Amazon Meksika'da RFC bildirmeyen satıcıdan yüzde 20 ISR stopajı ve yüzde 16 IVA kesintisi yapılır.

Türk satıcı için rota gerçekte nasıl işliyor?

Türkiye'den ABD'ye deniz veya hava, ABD deposunda konsolidasyon, kara sınırından geçiş, Meksika gümrüğünde pedimento ile ithalat, iç dağıtım.

Türkiye'den Meksika'ya doğrudan ticari hat sınırlı ve pahalı olduğu için pratikte kullanılan yol ABD üzerinden geçiyor. Mal Türkiye'den ABD'ye geliyor, Teksas'ta bir depoda konsolide ediliyor, oradan kara sınırından Meksika'ya geçiriliyor. Bu rotanın avantajı gerçek: taşıma maliyeti düşüyor, sipariş bazlı değil toplu geçiş yapılıyor, Meksika içi teslimat süresi kısalıyor ve iade adresi olarak ABD deposu kullanılabiliyor. Dezavantajı ise çoğu satıcının önceden hesaplamadığı bir yerde ortaya çıkıyor: iki ayrı ithalat var. Malı ABD'ye soktuğunuzda bir ithalat, ABD'den Meksika'ya soktuğunuzda ikinci bir ithalat yapıyorsunuz. Her ikisinin de kendi beyanı, kendi vergisi ve kendi belge seti var. Bu yüzden ABD deposu bir 'ara durak' değil, ayrı bir gümrük işlemidir. Maliyet hesabınızı buna göre kurmazsanız kâr marjınız gümrükte erir.

USMCA neden bizi kapsamıyor?

Çünkü USMCA menşe kurallarına dayanır ve Türkiye anlaşmanın tarafı değildir. Menşe, malın nerede üretildiğine bakar; nereden sevk edildiğine değil.

Bu, Türk satıcıların en sık ve en pahalı yanıldığı konu. Mantık şöyle kuruluyor: 'Malım ABD'de, ABD ile Meksika arasında serbest ticaret anlaşması var, o zaman gümrüksüz geçer.' Bu çıkarım yanlış. USMCA tercihli tarifesi malın menşeine bakar. Menşe, ürünün nerede üretildiği veya esaslı biçimde dönüştürüldüğüyle belirlenir. Türkiye'de üretilmiş bir ürün Teksas'ta altı ay depoda beklese de Meksika gümrüğü açısından Türk menşelidir. Depolamak, etiketlemek, yeniden paketlemek veya kutuya koymak esaslı dönüşüm sayılmaz. Sonuç olarak Türk menşeli ürün Meksika'ya girerken kendi tarife pozisyonunun genel oranını öder. Bu oran ürüne göre değişir ve sıfır da olabilir, yüksek de. Belirleyen şey ürünün GTİP/HS kodudur. Pratik sonuç şu: ABD deposu size lojistik ve operasyonel avantaj sağlar, gümrük avantajı sağlamaz. Fiyatlamanızı bu gerçeğin üzerine kurun. USMCA muafiyeti varmış gibi hesap yapıp sonra vergiyi marjdan karşılamak zorunda kalan çok satıcı gördük.

Meksika'ya ithalat yapmak için neye ihtiyacım var?

RFC sahibi bir Meksika tüzel kişiliği, ithalatçı siciline kayıt ve lisanslı gümrük müşaviri. Yabancı şirket kendi adına ithalat yapamaz.

Meksika'ya ticari ithalatta kayıtlı ithalatçı bir Meksika vergi mükellefi olmak zorundadır. Türkiye'deki şirketiniz kendi adına Meksika'ya ithalat yapamaz. Bu bir formalite değil, yasal bir kısıttır. Üç yol var. Birincisi Meksika'da şirket kurmak: tam kontrol sağlar ama aylar sürer ve sürekli vergi yükümlülüğü doğurur. İkincisi Meksikalı alıcıya DDP satmak: en basiti ama gümrük sürecinin kontrolünü kaybedersiniz. Üçüncüsü kayıtlı ithalatçı hizmeti almak, yani bir Meksika tüzel kişiliğinin sizin adınıza ithalatçı olarak görünmesi. Amazon Meksika'da satan Türk satıcıların çoğu üçüncü yolu kullanıyor; Amazon'un yabancı satıcıdan istediği FIOR tam olarak budur. Meşru ve yaygın bir yapıdır ama gerçek bir hukuki ilişkidir: kayıtlı ithalatçı, beyan edilenin doğruluğundan Meksika gümrüğüne karşı sorumludur. Vergi tarafında da bilmeniz gereken bir şey var: Amazon Meksika, RFC bildirmeyen satıcıdan yüzde 20 ISR stopajı yapıyor ve IVA'nın tamamını, yani yüzde 16'yı kesiyor. RFC'siz çalışmak sadece uyum sorunu değil, doğrudan nakit akışı sorunudur.

Maliyet kalemleri ve gerçek süreler

Navlun, gümrük müşavirliği, ithalat vergisi, yüzde 16 IVA ve DTA. Teksas'tan Meksika'nın merkezine 3-5 iş günü, belgeler tamsa.

Teklif karşılaştırırken kalemleri ayırmadan bakmak en yaygın hata. Ucuz görünen navlun, müşavirlik ve elleçlemeyi dışarıda bırakıyor olabilir. Navlun taşımanın kendisidir ve ABD içi çekiş, sınır geçişi ve Meksika içi taşımanın toplamı olabilir. Gümrük müşavirliği ücreti pedimento hazırlama ve beyan hizmetinin karşılığıdır, vergiden ayrıdır. İthalat vergisi HS koduna ve menşeye bağlıdır. IVA yüzde 16'dır ve gümrük değeri artı ithalat vergisi üzerinden hesaplanır, yani vergi verginin matrahını büyütür. DTA gümrük işlem hakkıdır. Sonra tekliflerde hiç görünmeyen kalemler geliyor: fiziki muayeneye düşerseniz muayene masrafı, mal beklerse ardiye, pedimento düzeltmesi gerekirse rektifikasyon. Sürelere gelince: Laredo-Monterrey yaklaşık 230 km, Laredo-Meksiko yaklaşık 1.100 km. Ama teslim tarihinizi belirleyen mesafe değil, gümrükte geçen süre. Belgeleri tam, sınıflandırması doğru bir sevkiyat bir günden kısa sürede geçer. Eksik izinli veya değeri sorgulanan bir sevkiyat bir hafta bekleyebilir. Planlamada 3-5 iş günü varsayın, ilk sevkiyatlar ve düzenlemeye tabi kategoriler için pay bırakın.

Hangi belgeler gerekiyor ve 1 Ağustos'ta ne değişti?

Ticari fatura, çeki listesi, taşıma belgesi, pedimento ve elektronik Değer Beyanı. 1 Ağustos 2026'dan itibaren Değer Beyanı VUTCE üzerinden elektronik zorunlu.

Ticari fatura savunulabilir bir işlem değeri ve açık bir mal tanımı içermelidir. 'Numune', 'yedek parça' gibi belirsiz tanımlar değer sorgulamasını davet eder. Pedimento Meksika gümrük beyannamesidir ve işlemin nihai hukuki kaydıdır. Sonraki bir denetimde sizden istenecek belge budur. Değer Beyanı, gümrük değerini destekleyen yeminli beyandır ve şu anda en acil başlık. SAT'ın 2 Haziran 2026'da yayımladığı düzenlemeyle kağıt formatla birlikte var olma süresi 31 Temmuz 2026'da sona erdi. 1 Ağustos 2026'dan itibaren beyanın VUTCE üzerinden elektronik verilmesi zorunlu. Hâlâ kağıt formatla çalışan bir tedarik zinciriniz varsa bu hafta içinde geçiş yapmış olmanız gerekiyordu. Düzenlemeye tabi kategoriler ek katman getirir: gıda, takviye, kozmetik ve tıbbi cihazlar için COFEPRIS izni; birçok tüketici ürünü için NOM belgelendirmesi ve İspanyolca etiketleme. Bunların hepsi HS koduyla belirlenir. Bu yüzden sınıflandırma en son değil, en başta yapılması gereken iştir.

Türk satıcı için üç ithalat yapısı

YapıNasıl işlerKime uygun
Meksika'da şirket kurmakKendi tüzel kişiliğiniz RFC alır ve ithalatçı siciline kaydolurYüksek hacim, uzun vadeli pazar taahhüdü
Meksikalı alıcıya DDP satışMüşteriniz kendi adına ithalat yaparYapısı hazır ithalatçılara B2B satış
Kayıtlı ithalatçı hizmeti (FIOR)Bir Meksika tüzel kişiliği sizin adınıza ithalatçı olurYerel şirketi olmayan e-ticaret ve Amazon satıcıları

Tanımlar

  • Pedimento: Pedimento, Meksika'da her ithalat ve ihracat için düzenlenen resmî gümrük beyannamesidir ve beyan edilen, sınıflandırılan ve ödenen her şeyin hukuki kaydıdır.
  • Menşe: Menşe, ürünün nerede üretildiği veya esaslı biçimde dönüştürüldüğüdür; nereden sevk edildiği menşei değiştirmez.
  • FIOR: FIOR, yerel tüzel kişiliği olmayan yabancı satıcı adına Meksika'da kayıtlı ithalatçı sıfatıyla hareket eden yapıdır.

Sık sorulan sorular

Türk ürünü ABD deposunda beklerse USMCA muafiyetinden yararlanır mı?

Hayır. USMCA tercihli tarifesi menşeye bakar ve Türkiye anlaşmanın tarafı değildir. Türkiye'de üretilmiş ürün ABD'de ne kadar beklerse beklesin Türk menşeli kalır. Depolama, etiketleme ve yeniden paketleme esaslı dönüşüm sayılmaz.

Türkiye'deki şirketimle Meksika'ya ithalat yapabilir miyim?

Hayır. Meksika'ya ticari ithalatta kayıtlı ithalatçının RFC sahibi bir Meksika tüzel kişiliği olması ve ithalatçı siciline kayıtlı olması gerekir. Meksika'da şirket kurmak, DDP satmak veya kayıtlı ithalatçı hizmeti almak seçenekleriniz var.

Amazon Meksika RFC vermezsem ne kadar kesinti yapar?

RFC bildirilmediğinde yüzde 20 ISR stopajı uygulanır ve IVA'nın tamamı, yani yüzde 16, kesilir. Bu, uyum sorununun ötesinde doğrudan bir nakit akışı sorunudur.

Teksas'tan Meksika'ya sevkiyat ne kadar sürer?

Belgeler tamsa Meksika'nın merkezine 3-5 iş günü. Belirleyici olan mesafe değil gümrükte geçen süredir. Eksik belge veya sorgulanan değer süreyi bir haftanın üzerine çıkarabilir.

1 Ağustos 2026'da ne değişti?

Değer Beyanı'nın VUTCE üzerinden elektronik verilmesi zorunlu hale geldi. Kağıt formatla birlikte var olma süresi 31 Temmuz 2026'da sona erdi; bu, SAT'ın 2 Haziran 2026 tarihli düzenlemesiyle belirlenmişti.

IVA neyin üzerinden hesaplanır?

Yüzde 16'lık IVA, sadece fatura değeri üzerinden değil, gümrük değeri artı ithalat vergisi üzerinden hesaplanır. Yani ithalat vergisi IVA'nın matrahını da büyütür.

translations.title: Do Trucks Get Inspected When Crossing Into Mexico?
translations.excerpt: Mexican customs does not inspect every truck, and it does not choose at random in the way most shippers assume. Understanding the selection mechanism tells you what you can and cannot control.
translations.content:
Not every truck is inspected. Mexico uses an automated selection mechanism at clearance that designates a portion of shipments for reconocimiento aduanero, a physical and documentary examination. Shipments not selected are released without examination. Selection is partly randomised and partly risk-based, so importers with clean classification, consistent values and complete documentation face both fewer examinations and much shorter ones when selected.

  • Mexico's clearance process runs an automated selection mechanism that determines whether a shipment receives reconocimiento aduanero.
  • Reconocimiento aduanero covers both the physical goods and the documentation, checking that what arrived matches what was declared.
  • Selection is not purely random; risk profiling considers importer history, product category, declared value and origin.
  • A shipment that matches its declaration clears examination quickly; discrepancies trigger sampling, valuation review or seizure.
  • From 1 August 2026, an incomplete electronic Manifestación de Valor is itself a documentary problem, since the filing became mandatory through the single window.

How does Mexico decide which trucks to inspect?

An automated selection mechanism runs at clearance and designates a share of shipments for examination, combining randomisation with risk profiling.

When your customs broker files the pedimento and the shipment is presented, an automated system determines whether the shipment proceeds directly or goes to reconocimiento aduanero. This is not a customs officer deciding on sight. The randomised component means that even a perfectly compliant importer will occasionally be selected. You cannot engineer your way out of it, and you should not try. The risk-profiling component is where your behaviour matters: importer history, the product category, the declared value relative to what customs expects for that classification, and the origin of the goods all feed the profile. The practical implication is that an importer's inspection rate is not fixed. A first-time importer bringing in a category that is commonly undervalued will see more examinations than an established importer with a consistent record in a low-risk category. That record is built over time and it is an asset worth protecting.

What happens during an inspection?

Officials verify that the physical goods match the declaration: quantity, description, classification, and value support.

An examination checks correspondence. The officer compares the goods against the pedimento, the commercial invoice and the packing list. Quantity, description, and whether the classification fits the goods as they actually are. Most examinations that go badly go badly for mundane reasons. Cartons contain more units than the packing list says. The invoice describes 'electronic accessories' and the carton contains something with a specific regulatory requirement. The declared value is far below what the classification usually carries and there is no documentation supporting why. When a discrepancy appears, the consequences scale with the type. A minor documentary error may be corrected through a pedimento rectification with a fee and a delay. A valuation dispute opens a review that can hold the shipment for an extended period. A regulatory violation, such as goods requiring COFEPRIS authorisation or NOM certification that were declared as something else, can result in seizure. The shipments that clear examination fastest are the boring ones: what was declared is what is in the trailer.

What can a shipper actually control?

Classification accuracy, description precision, value documentation and completeness of the file. Not selection itself.

Start with classification, because it determines everything downstream. The HS code decides the duty rate, whether a permit or NOM certification applies, and what the customs system expects the value to look like. Getting it wrong does not just cost duty; it can put you in a category where you had no idea a permit was required. Write descriptions that a person can verify by opening a box. 'Cotton t-shirts, men's, short sleeve, 180gsm' is verifiable. 'Apparel' is not, and it invites questions. Keep value documentation with the file, not in someone's inbox. Purchase orders, payment records and price lists supporting the declared transaction value should be retrievable while the truck is at the border, not a week later. And make sure the Manifestación de Valor is filed electronically. Since 1 August 2026 this is mandatory through the single window that ANAM's 2026 communications call VUTCE, the successor to VUCEM. A missing value manifest converts a routine examination into a documentary failure. What you cannot control is selection. Build a schedule that tolerates an occasional examination rather than one that assumes every shipment sails through.

What determines examination outcome

FactorUnder your controlEffect if wrong
Selection for examinationNoAdds time regardless of compliance
HS classificationYesWrong duty, missed permits, valuation flags
Goods descriptionYesQuestioning, sampling, delay
Value documentationYesValuation review, extended hold
Electronic value manifestYesDocumentary non-compliance since 1 August 2026

Definitions

  • Reconocimiento aduanero: Reconocimiento aduanero is the physical and documentary examination of a shipment carried out when the automated selection mechanism designates it.
  • Pedimento rectification: A pedimento rectification is a formal correction to a filed customs declaration, which carries a fee and typically delays release.

Frequently asked questions

Are all trucks inspected at the Mexican border?

No. An automated selection mechanism designates a portion of shipments for reconocimiento aduanero. Shipments not selected are released without physical examination.

Can I avoid being selected for inspection?

No, because selection includes a randomised component. You can reduce your risk profile through accurate classification, precise descriptions and a consistent import history, but no importer is exempt.

How long does a customs examination take?

A shipment that matches its declaration is typically released the same day. Discrepancies extend this considerably: valuation reviews and regulatory issues can hold goods for a week or longer.

What is the most common reason inspections go wrong?

Mismatch between the declaration and the goods. Quantity differences, vague descriptions that hide a regulated product, and declared values without supporting documentation are the recurring causes.

translations.title: Amazon Mexico Tax Withholding For Foreign Sellers: IVA And ISR Explained
translations.excerpt: Selling on Amazon Mexico without a Mexican tax registration is not just a compliance gap. It is a direct and immediate hit to your cash flow, applied to every order.
translations.content:
Amazon Mexico withholds tax from marketplace sellers at source. A seller who has not provided a valid Mexican RFC faces the maximum rates: 20 percent ISR on the sale price and the full 16 percent IVA. Sellers with a registered RFC face substantially lower ISR withholding, and registered taxpayers can credit withheld IVA against their own liability. The withholding is applied by Amazon and remitted to SAT; it is not optional and it is not negotiable.

  • Without a valid RFC, ISR withholding is 20 percent of the sale price, applied regardless of your actual margin.
  • Without an RFC, or where funds are paid to a foreign bank account, platforms withhold 100 percent of the IVA, which at the standard rate means 16 percent.
  • Mexico's 2026 tax framework extended automatic withholding across digital platforms including Amazon and Mercado Libre, for both individuals and companies.
  • IVA withheld from a registered taxpayer can be credited; IVA withheld from an unregistered foreign seller generally cannot be recovered.
  • Withholding is calculated on the sale price, not on profit, which is why it hits low-margin categories hardest.

What does Amazon withhold and at what rate?

Two separate taxes. ISR at 20 percent of the sale price for sellers without an RFC, and IVA at the full 16 percent where no RFC is provided or funds go to a foreign account.

Mexico requires digital platforms to withhold tax at source from the sellers who trade on them. Amazon does not choose to do this; it is a legal obligation, and the amount depends on what you have told Amazon about your tax status. ISR is income tax. For a seller without a valid RFC the withholding is 20 percent of the sale price. Read that carefully: the sale price, not the profit. A seller running a 15 percent margin does not pay 20 percent of the margin, they lose more than the margin itself on that transaction. IVA is value added tax, standard rate 16 percent. Where the seller has not provided an RFC, or where proceeds are paid to a foreign bank account, the platform withholds the entire IVA rather than a partial share. The two stack. A seller without an RFC selling into Mexico sees both applied to the same transaction, and the combined effect is severe enough that many sellers discover their Mexico operation was never profitable once the first settlement report arrives.

Why does the RFC change the outcome so much?

The maximum rates function as a default for unidentified taxpayers. Registration moves you into the ordinary regime with lower rates and recoverable IVA.

The high withholding is not a penalty in the formal sense, but it works like one. Mexico's tax authority cannot assess a seller it cannot identify, so the system withholds at the top of the range and leaves it to the seller to register and reconcile. Once you have a valid RFC and the platform has it on file, two things change. ISR withholding falls to the rate applicable to your regime rather than the punitive default. And withheld IVA becomes creditable: as a registered taxpayer you offset it against the IVA you charge and owe, so it stops being a permanent cost and becomes a timing difference. For a foreign seller without Mexican registration, withheld IVA is generally not recoverable. That is the part sellers underestimate. The ISR is painful but visible; the unrecoverable IVA is a silent 16 percent that never comes back. This is why the RFC question is not a paperwork preference. It determines whether roughly a third of your revenue is a tax cost or a recoverable balance.

What are the options for a foreign seller?

Register a Mexican entity and obtain an RFC, work through a structure that holds the RFC, or accept the maximum withholding as a cost of doing business.

Establishing a Mexican entity gives you an RFC, access to the ordinary tax regime, creditable IVA and the ability to enrol in the padrón de importadores so you can import in your own name. The cost is time, professional fees and ongoing filing obligations, including monthly returns whether or not you traded. Operating through a structure that holds the Mexican tax registration is what many cross-border sellers use, particularly when combined with an importer of record arrangement. It resolves the import side and the tax registration together. It is a real commercial relationship, so understand who bears which liability before signing. Accepting the withholding is a legitimate short-term choice while you test the market, provided you price for it. What does not work is pricing as though the withholding is not there and hoping to fix it later. The withholding applies from your first order. Whichever route you choose, model it before you launch. Take a representative SKU, apply 20 percent ISR and 16 percent IVA to the sale price, subtract landed cost and Amazon's referral and fulfilment fees, and see what remains. That number, not the gross margin, is your Mexico business case.

Withholding by seller status

Seller statusISR withholdingIVA treatment
No RFC provided20 percent of sale priceFull 16 percent withheld, generally not recoverable
Proceeds to foreign bank accountApplies per regimeFull IVA withheld
Valid RFC, registered regimeRate per applicable regimeWithheld IVA creditable against liability

Definitions

  • RFC: The RFC (Registro Federal de Contribuyentes) is the Mexican tax identification number required for tax registration, importing and reduced platform withholding.
  • ISR: ISR (Impuesto Sobre la Renta) is Mexican income tax, withheld by marketplaces from seller proceeds at a rate that depends on the seller's registration status.
  • IVA: IVA (Impuesto al Valor Agregado) is Mexican value added tax at a standard rate of 16 percent, creditable by registered taxpayers and a sunk cost for unregistered foreign sellers.

Frequently asked questions

How much does Amazon Mexico withhold if I have no RFC?

20 percent ISR on the sale price plus the full 16 percent IVA. Both are calculated on the sale price rather than on profit, which is why the combined effect often exceeds a seller's gross margin.

Can I get the withheld IVA back?

A registered Mexican taxpayer can credit withheld IVA against IVA owed. A foreign seller without Mexican tax registration generally cannot recover it, so it becomes a permanent cost.

Do I need a Mexican company to get an RFC?

In practice, tax registration in Mexico requires either a Mexican legal entity or an individual with Mexican tax residency. Foreign sellers commonly work through a structure that holds the registration instead.

Is the withholding calculated on profit or on the sale price?

On the sale price. This is the detail that surprises most sellers, because a 20 percent withholding on revenue can exceed the entire margin on a low-margin product.

Does providing a bank account in Mexico change the withholding?

Paying proceeds to a foreign bank account triggers full IVA withholding. A Mexican account alone does not substitute for an RFC, but the combination of RFC and local account produces the ordinary treatment.

translations.title: What Is A Mexico RFC And Do You Need One?
translations.excerpt: The RFC sits underneath almost every Mexican commercial requirement: importing, invoicing, marketplace withholding. Knowing whether you need one is the first structural decision in a Mexico strategy.
translations.content:
The RFC (Registro Federal de Contribuyentes) is Mexico's tax identification number, issued by SAT to individuals and companies with Mexican tax obligations. You need one to enrol in the padrón de importadores and import commercially, to issue CFDI electronic invoices, and to avoid maximum marketplace withholding. A foreign company cannot obtain an RFC without establishing Mexican tax presence, which is why foreign sellers typically work through a structure that holds one.

  • The RFC is issued by SAT and is required for enrolment in the padrón de importadores, without which commercial importing is not possible.
  • Issuing a CFDI, Mexico's mandatory electronic invoice, requires an RFC and an active e.firma.
  • Marketplaces withhold at maximum rates from sellers who have not provided a valid RFC: 20 percent ISR and the full 16 percent IVA.
  • An RFC brings ongoing obligations, including periodic returns that must be filed whether or not there was activity in the period.
  • Enrolment in the padrón de importadores additionally requires a positive opinión de cumplimiento, so outstanding tax issues block the application.

What is the RFC and what does it unlock?

It is Mexico's tax ID, and it is the prerequisite for importing, invoicing, and being treated as an ordinary taxpayer rather than an unidentified one.

The RFC is the identifier SAT uses for every taxpayer in Mexico. Structurally it is similar to a tax identification number elsewhere, but its practical reach in commercial operations is wider than most foreign sellers expect. Three things depend on it. Importing: enrolment in the padrón de importadores requires an RFC, and without padrón enrolment you cannot be the importer of record on a commercial shipment. Invoicing: Mexican business customers require a CFDI, the electronic invoice, to deduct their purchase, and issuing one requires an RFC and a valid e.firma. Withholding: marketplaces apply maximum rates to sellers without an RFC. There is a fourth, less obvious effect. Mexican B2B buyers frequently will not transact with a supplier who cannot issue a CFDI, because the purchase becomes non-deductible for them. This is not a preference; it is an accounting consequence. If your Mexico plan involves selling to businesses, the RFC is not optional in any practical sense.

Can a foreign company get an RFC?

Not without Mexican tax presence. In practice this means a Mexican legal entity, a permanent establishment, or working through a structure that already holds one.

An RFC is issued to taxpayers with Mexican tax obligations. A company incorporated in the United States, Turkey or Spain with no Mexican presence does not have those obligations and cannot simply apply. The routes that do work are three. Incorporating a Mexican entity, typically an S. de R.L. or S.A. de C.V., which then obtains its own RFC. Registering a permanent establishment, which is appropriate in narrower circumstances and carries its own tax consequences. Or contracting with a Mexican entity that acts as importer of record and, where relevant, as the invoicing party. The third is what most cross-border e-commerce sellers use, and it is what Amazon expects when it asks a foreign seller for a FIOR. It is legitimate. It is also a genuine allocation of legal responsibility: the Mexican entity is answerable to SAT and to customs for what is declared under its registration, which is why these arrangements are contractual rather than casual. The wrong approach is to borrow someone's RFC informally. The registration carries liability, and using another party's registration without a proper arrangement exposes both sides.

What does having an RFC oblige you to do?

File periodic returns, maintain a positive compliance opinion, keep the fiscal address current, and hold a valid e.firma.

An RFC is not a one-time registration you obtain and forget. It creates recurring obligations, and the cost of neglecting them shows up at the worst moment. Periodic returns must be filed even for periods with no activity. A dormant entity that stops filing accumulates omissions, and those omissions turn the opinión de cumplimiento negative. That compliance opinion matters more than it sounds. It is required for padrón de importadores enrolment and is checked for various procedures. An importer who lets it lapse can find shipments blocked not because of anything wrong with the shipment, but because a return was missed months earlier. The e.firma, Mexico's advanced electronic signature, must be kept valid. It expires, and renewal requires an appointment. Companies discover this when they need to file something urgently and cannot. The fiscal address must be real and locatable. SAT verifies addresses, and a domicile that cannot be verified can move the taxpayer status to non-localised, which cascades into the compliance opinion. None of this is onerous with a competent Mexican accountant. All of it is expensive to fix retroactively.

Routes to Mexican tax registration

RouteTimelineSuits
Incorporate a Mexican entityMonths, plus ongoing filingsCommitted market entry, own-name importing
Work through an importer of recordDays to weeksE-commerce and marketplace sellers
Sell DDP to a Mexican buyerImmediateB2B where the buyer already has structure

Definitions

  • e.firma: The e.firma is Mexico's advanced electronic signature, required for filing returns, issuing invoices and completing SAT procedures, and it expires and must be renewed.
  • Opinión de cumplimiento: The opinión de cumplimiento is SAT's compliance status certificate, which must be positive for padrón enrolment and various other procedures.
  • CFDI: A CFDI is Mexico's mandatory electronic invoice, which Mexican business buyers require in order to deduct a purchase.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need an RFC to sell on Amazon Mexico?

You can sell without one, but Amazon will withhold at maximum rates: 20 percent ISR and the full 16 percent IVA. Without Mexican tax registration the withheld IVA is generally not recoverable.

Can a US or Turkish company obtain a Mexican RFC?

Not directly. An RFC requires Mexican tax obligations, which means a Mexican entity or permanent establishment. Foreign sellers commonly work through a Mexican entity acting as importer of record instead.

Do I need an RFC to import into Mexico?

Yes. Enrolment in the padrón de importadores requires an RFC, and commercial imports require padrón enrolment. The importer of record must therefore be a Mexican registered taxpayer.

What happens if I have an RFC but stop filing?

Omitted returns turn your opinión de cumplimiento negative, which can block padrón enrolment and other procedures. Returns must be filed even for periods with no activity.

translations.title: Shipping Lithium Batteries To Mexico: UN38.3 And Transport Rules
translations.excerpt: Lithium batteries sit at the intersection of dangerous goods rules and Mexican product certification. Sellers who treat them as ordinary electronics discover both sets of requirements at the border.
translations.content:
Lithium batteries are Class 9 dangerous goods and require a UN38.3 test report, a safety data sheet, compliant packaging and Class 9 marking for transport into Mexico. On the Mexican import side, batteries fall under NOM requirements including NOM-212-SCFI-2017, which limits mercury and cadmium content. For air transport, lithium ion cells and batteries shipped standalone must be offered at a reduced state of charge, and from 1 January 2026 this extends to batteries packed with equipment.

  • UN38.3 is the United Nations transport test standard; a valid test report is required before lithium cells or batteries may be transported.
  • Lithium batteries are classified as Class 9 dangerous goods and require corresponding packaging, marking and documentation.
  • NOM-212-SCFI-2017 sets maximum permitted mercury and cadmium content by weight for batteries placed on the Mexican market.
  • From 1 January 2026, lithium ion batteries packed with equipment, and vehicles powered by lithium ion or sodium ion batteries, must also be offered at a reduced state of charge unless approved otherwise.
  • Products subject to NOMs generally must demonstrate compliance before customs release, although border verification options exist in some cases.

What documentation does a lithium battery shipment need?

A UN38.3 test report, a safety data sheet, a dangerous goods declaration where applicable, and packaging and marking that match the classification.

The UN38.3 test report is the foundational document. It certifies that the cell or battery has passed the United Nations transport tests covering conditions such as altitude simulation, thermal cycling, vibration, shock, external short circuit and impact. Without it, compliant carriers will not accept the goods. A safety data sheet accompanies the shipment and describes the chemistry, hazards and handling requirements. Packaging must match the classification. Lithium batteries are Class 9, and the applicable packing instruction depends on whether cells are shipped alone, packed with equipment, or contained in equipment, and on watt-hour rating. Marking and labelling follow from that. One practical warning: the UN38.3 report belongs to the cell or battery model, and it comes from the manufacturer. If your supplier cannot produce it, that is a sourcing problem you must solve before you have inventory, not a paperwork step you can complete afterwards. Sellers who buy first and ask for documentation later frequently find the report does not exist for that specific model.

What does Mexico require on the import side?

NOM compliance in addition to transport rules, including NOM-212-SCFI-2017 on heavy metal content, and Spanish-language labelling where applicable.

Transport compliance gets the goods to the border. Mexican product regulation determines whether they may enter the market. Batteries placed on the Mexican market fall within the NOM framework. NOM-212-SCFI-2017 sets maximum permitted mercury and cadmium content by weight. Depending on the product and its classification, other NOMs may apply, including requirements relevant to electronic products and their labelling. Products subject to NOM requirements generally need to demonstrate compliance before customs release. In some circumstances verification at the border is available rather than certification in advance, but this depends on the specific NOM and the product, and it is not something to assume. As with everything in Mexican customs, the HS classification determines which requirements attach. A battery shipped as a component within a device may face different requirements from the same battery shipped standalone. Establish the classification first, then work out the regulatory consequences, rather than the other way round.

What about state of charge and air transport?

Standalone lithium ion cells and batteries must be offered at a reduced state of charge for air transport, and from 1 January 2026 this extends to batteries packed with equipment.

State of charge limits exist because a fully charged lithium cell carries more energy to release in a thermal event. For air transport, standalone lithium ion cells and batteries have been subject to a reduced state of charge requirement, commonly implemented as not more than 30 percent of rated capacity. From 1 January 2026 the scope widened. Lithium ion batteries packed with equipment, and vehicles powered by lithium ion or sodium ion batteries, must also be offered at a reduced state of charge unless the relevant States have approved otherwise. This matters for planning because it affects what you can send by air and how your supplier must prepare the goods. A shipment prepared at full charge is not a documentation problem you can fix at the airport; it is a physical condition of the goods. Ground transport across the US-Mexico land border follows dangerous goods rules for road rather than the air regime, but the underlying UN38.3 and packaging requirements still apply, and Mexican product certification requirements apply regardless of transport mode. Confirm the specific requirements for your battery type, watt-hour rating and packing configuration with your carrier before you book.

Requirement layers for lithium batteries into Mexico

LayerRequirementSource
Transport testUN38.3 test report per cell or battery modelUN Manual of Tests and Criteria
Dangerous goodsClass 9 packaging, marking, documentationModal dangerous goods regulations
Air state of chargeReduced state of charge; scope widened 1 January 2026IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations
Mexican product ruleMercury and cadmium limitsNOM-212-SCFI-2017
Market entryNOM compliance demonstrated for customs releaseMexican NOM framework

Definitions

  • UN38.3: UN38.3 is the United Nations transport test standard for lithium cells and batteries, and a valid test report is a prerequisite for compliant transport.
  • NOM: A NOM (Norma Oficial Mexicana) is a mandatory Mexican technical standard, and products subject to one generally must demonstrate compliance for customs release.
  • State of charge: State of charge is the proportion of a battery's rated capacity that is charged, and air transport rules limit it for lithium ion cells and batteries.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a UN38.3 report to ship batteries to Mexico?

Yes. UN38.3 testing is the transport prerequisite for lithium cells and batteries, and the test report is model-specific and comes from the manufacturer. Compliant carriers will not accept the goods without it.

Are lithium batteries dangerous goods?

Yes, they are Class 9 dangerous goods, which brings packaging, marking and documentation requirements that depend on watt-hour rating and whether cells ship standalone, with equipment, or in equipment.

What is NOM-212-SCFI-2017?

It is the Mexican standard setting maximum permitted mercury and cadmium content by weight for batteries placed on the Mexican market.

What changed for lithium batteries on 1 January 2026?

The reduced state of charge requirement for air transport widened to include lithium ion batteries packed with equipment and vehicles powered by lithium ion or sodium ion batteries, unless the relevant States approve otherwise.

Can I ship batteries by truck instead to avoid the rules?

Road transport follows its own dangerous goods regime rather than the air rules, but UN38.3 testing, Class 9 packaging and Mexican NOM requirements still apply. Changing mode changes some rules, not the requirement to comply.

translations.title: FIOR: El Foreign Importer Of Record Que Amazon Te Pide
translations.excerpt: Amazon pide un FIOR y muchos vendedores lo tratan como un dato más del formulario. Es una figura con responsabilidad legal real frente a la aduana mexicana, y conviene entender quién responde por qué.
translations.content:
El FIOR (Foreign Importer of Record) es la figura mediante la cual una entidad mexicana actúa como importador registrado por cuenta de un vendedor extranjero que no tiene presencia fiscal en México. Permite importar sin constituir una empresa mexicana, pero la entidad que funge como importador asume responsabilidad frente a la autoridad aduanera por la exactitud de lo declarado. No es un trámite administrativo: es una relación jurídica con obligaciones reales para ambas partes.

  • Una empresa extranjera no puede ser importador registrado en México; el importador debe tener RFC e inscripción en el padrón de importadores.
  • El FIOR permite operar sin constituir entidad mexicana, pero la responsabilidad aduanera recae en la entidad mexicana que funge como importador.
  • Amazon solicita esta figura a vendedores extranjeros precisamente porque la plataforma no puede ser el importador de la mercancía de terceros.
  • El pedimento se emite a nombre del importador registrado, no del vendedor extranjero.
  • Desde el 1 de agosto de 2026, la Manifestación de Valor que sustenta el valor declarado debe presentarse electrónicamente, y esa obligación corresponde al importador.

¿Qué es exactamente un FIOR?

Una entidad mexicana con RFC y padrón que funge como importador registrado por cuenta de un vendedor extranjero sin presencia fiscal en México.

El punto de partida es una restricción legal: en México el importador registrado tiene que ser un contribuyente mexicano inscrito en el padrón de importadores. Una empresa estadounidense, turca o española sin presencia fiscal en el país no puede serlo. El FIOR resuelve ese problema. Una entidad mexicana con RFC vigente y padrón activo aparece como importador en el pedimento, y la mercancía del vendedor extranjero entra legalmente al país. Lo que conviene entender es qué se transfiere y qué no. La titularidad comercial de la mercancía puede seguir siendo del vendedor extranjero. La responsabilidad aduanera, en cambio, corre por cuenta de la entidad que aparece como importador: es quien responde ante la autoridad por la clasificación arancelaria, el valor declarado, el cumplimiento de regulaciones no arancelarias y la conservación de la documentación. Por eso un FIOR serio pide información detallada antes de aceptar una operación. Si alguien ofrece el servicio sin preguntar qué va dentro de las cajas, esa señal dice más de lo que parece.

¿Por qué Amazon lo exige?

Porque Amazon no importa la mercancía de sus vendedores. Necesita que exista un importador registrado identificable para la mercancía que llega a sus centros.

Cuando un vendedor extranjero manda inventario a un centro de Amazon en México, alguien tiene que haberlo importado. Amazon no asume esa función: recibe y almacena mercancía que ya entró al país legalmente. Por eso la plataforma pide al vendedor extranjero que identifique quién es su importador registrado. No es un requisito interno de Amazon; es el reflejo de la exigencia legal mexicana en el flujo operativo de la plataforma. Esto explica también por qué un vendedor no puede enviar directamente desde Estados Unidos a un centro logístico mexicano sin resolver antes la estructura de importación. La mercancía tiene que despacharse antes de llegar, con pedimento a nombre de un importador registrado. Y conviene ligarlo con el tema fiscal, porque van juntos. El vendedor sin RFC sufre retención de 20 por ciento de ISR y del 16 por ciento de IVA completo sobre sus ventas. Resolver la importación mediante FIOR y no resolver el RFC deja el problema fiscal intacto. Son dos decisiones distintas y ambas tienen que tomarse.

¿Qué debe revisar antes de contratar un FIOR?

Que el padrón esté activo, quién responde ante una revisión, cómo se maneja la documentación de valor y qué pasa con las devoluciones.

Primero, verifique que la entidad tenga padrón de importadores activo y opinión de cumplimiento positiva. Un padrón suspendido detiene sus embarques sin previo aviso y usted se entera cuando la mercancía ya está en la frontera. Segundo, defina por contrato quién responde ante una revisión posterior. La autoridad puede revisar operaciones tiempo después del despacho. Si aparece una diferencia de clasificación o de valor, el importador registrado es el sujeto obligado, pero la relación entre ustedes determina quién absorbe el costo. Eso se pacta antes, no cuando llega el requerimiento. Tercero, aclare el manejo de la documentación de valor. Desde el 1 de agosto de 2026 la Manifestación de Valor debe presentarse electrónicamente por la ventanilla única que la ANAM denomina VUTCE en sus comunicados de 2026. Esa obligación es del importador, y quien la cumple necesita información veraz de usted: facturas, órdenes de compra, evidencia de pago. Si usted no entrega esa información, está pidiéndole a alguien que declare bajo protesta algo que no puede sustentar. Cuarto, resuelva las devoluciones desde el inicio. La mercancía que entra bajo un FIOR y luego se devuelve o se retorna tiene su propio tratamiento aduanero. Es más barato diseñarlo que improvisarlo.

Quién responde por qué en un esquema FIOR

AspectoVendedor extranjeroImportador registrado (FIOR)
Titularidad de la mercancíaNormalmente conservaNo necesariamente
Nombre en el pedimentoNo aparece como importadorAparece como importador
Responsabilidad ante la aduanaIndirecta, vía contratoDirecta
Veracidad de la información de valorDebe proporcionarlaDebe declararla
Manifestación de Valor electrónicaAporta sustentoObligado a presentarla

Definiciones

  • Importador registrado: El importador registrado es la persona inscrita en el padrón de importadores a cuyo nombre se emite el pedimento y que responde ante la autoridad por la operación.
  • Padrón de importadores: El padrón de importadores es el registro del SAT sin el cual no puede realizarse una importación comercial a México.

Preguntas frecuentes

¿Puedo importar a México sin constituir empresa mexicana?

Sí, mediante un esquema de importador registrado como el FIOR, en el que una entidad mexicana con RFC y padrón funge como importador por cuenta de usted. También puede vender DDP a un comprador mexicano que importe en su nombre.

¿Quién responde si la aduana detecta un error de clasificación?

Ante la autoridad responde el importador registrado, porque el pedimento se emite a su nombre. Cómo se distribuye ese costo entre usted y el FIOR depende de lo que hayan pactado por contrato.

¿El FIOR resuelve también mi situación fiscal en Amazon?

No. Son dos cosas distintas. El FIOR resuelve la importación; la retención de Amazon depende de si usted proporcionó un RFC válido. Sin RFC la retención sigue siendo de 20 por ciento de ISR y del IVA completo.

¿Qué pasa con la Manifestación de Valor?

Es obligación del importador y desde el 1 de agosto de 2026 debe presentarse electrónicamente. El importador necesita que usted le entregue facturas y evidencia de pago que sustenten el valor declarado.

  • ANAM — Agencia Nacional de Aduanas de México (anam.gob.mx)

translations.title: Cómo Leer Un Pedimento Campo Por Campo
translations.excerpt: La mayoría de los importadores archiva el pedimento sin leerlo. Es el documento que la autoridad le pedirá en una revisión y el que determina si pagó de más o de menos.
translations.content:
El pedimento es la declaración aduanera oficial de una operación de comercio exterior en México. Se organiza en bloques: datos del importador y del agente aduanal, régimen y tipo de operación, datos del transporte, valor en aduana y su determinación, fracciones arancelarias por partida, y liquidación de contribuciones. Revíselo antes de que se archive: la clasificación arancelaria y el valor declarado son los dos campos que determinan cuánto pagó y qué tan expuesto está en una revisión posterior.

  • El pedimento es el registro legal de la operación y es lo que la autoridad solicita en cualquier revisión posterior al despacho.
  • La fracción arancelaria determina el arancel aplicable y también qué regulaciones no arancelarias se activan.
  • El valor en aduana no es sólo el precio de factura: incorpora incrementables como flete y seguro hasta el punto de entrada.
  • El IVA de importación se calcula sobre el valor en aduana más el impuesto general de importación, por lo que el arancel amplía la base.
  • Desde el 1 de agosto de 2026 la Manifestación de Valor que sustenta ese valor se presenta de forma electrónica obligatoria.

¿Qué bloques componen un pedimento?

Identificación de las partes, régimen aduanero, transporte, valor y su determinación, partidas con su fracción arancelaria, y la liquidación de contribuciones.

El pedimento parece denso porque lo es, pero está organizado por bloques y cada bloque responde a una pregunta. El bloque de identificación dice quién importa y quién despacha: el RFC del importador registrado y los datos del agente aduanal. Si el nombre del importador no es el que usted espera, deténgase ahí y pregunte. El bloque de régimen indica qué tipo de operación es: importación definitiva, temporal, retorno. El régimen cambia por completo las obligaciones posteriores, y una importación temporal mal cerrada se convierte en un problema fiscal meses después. El bloque de transporte registra el medio, el transportista y los datos del cruce. El bloque de valor es el más importante y el que menos gente lee. Contiene el valor en aduana, el valor comercial y los incrementables. El bloque de partidas desglosa la mercancía: cada partida lleva su descripción, su fracción arancelaria, cantidad y valor. Y el bloque de liquidación suma lo que se pagó: impuesto general de importación, IVA, DTA y cualquier otra contribución. Ese total debe cuadrar con lo que su agente le cobró. Si trabaja con un agente aduanal, pídale la guía de campos de su sistema. Cada uno numera los apartados conforme al formato vigente y es más útil revisar el suyo que memorizar un esquema genérico.

¿Qué debo revisar sí o sí?

La fracción arancelaria, la descripción de la mercancía, el valor en aduana y el régimen. Esos cuatro campos concentran casi todo el riesgo.

La fracción arancelaria es el campo que más dinero mueve. Determina el arancel, y también si su mercancía necesita permiso, NOM o inscripción en un padrón sectorial. Una fracción incorrecta no sólo cambia lo que paga: puede significar que importó sin un permiso que sí requería. La descripción debe corresponder con lo que realmente venía. Si el pedimento dice una cosa y la caja contiene otra, ese desfase es exactamente lo que se detecta en un reconocimiento aduanero. El valor en aduana debe ser sustentable con documentos. No es únicamente el precio de la factura: incorpora incrementables. Si su agente declaró un valor y usted no tiene cómo respaldarlo con orden de compra y evidencia de pago, tiene una contingencia abierta. El régimen determina qué le toca hacer después. Una importación temporal tiene plazo de retorno; si vence sin regularizarse, se convierte en una omisión. Un hábito que ahorra dinero: revise el pedimento el mismo día que lo recibe, no cuando llegue un requerimiento. Las rectificaciones son más baratas y más simples cuando se hacen a tiempo.

¿Qué errores salen más caros?

Clasificación incorrecta, valor sin sustento y régimen mal elegido. Los tres se detectan tarde y se corrigen caro.

La clasificación incorrecta es el error más común. A veces es a la baja, y entonces hay omisión de contribuciones. A veces es a la alta, y entonces pagó de más sin saberlo. En ambos casos, cuando la autoridad revisa, la diferencia se determina con actualizaciones y recargos. El valor sin sustento aparece cuando el precio declarado no puede documentarse. Aquí conviene ser claro: subvaluar no es una estrategia, es una contingencia. La autoridad tiene mecanismos para cuestionar valores que se apartan de lo esperado para esa fracción, y la carga de demostrar el valor de transacción es del importador. El régimen mal elegido suele venir de operaciones que se plantearon como temporales y terminaron siendo definitivas de facto. La mercancía se quedó, el plazo venció, nadie regularizó. Y hay un cuarto que ahora tiene fecha: la documentación de valor. Desde el 1 de agosto de 2026 la Manifestación de Valor debe presentarse electrónicamente por la ventanilla única que la ANAM denomina VUTCE en sus comunicados de 2026. Un expediente que no puede sustentar el valor declarado ya no sólo es débil ante una revisión: incumple una obligación con fecha cierta.

Los cuatro campos de mayor riesgo

CampoQué determinaSi está mal
Fracción arancelariaArancel, permisos, NOM, padrón sectorialOmisión de contribuciones o importación sin permiso
Descripción de mercancíaCorrespondencia con lo físicoDiscrepancia en reconocimiento aduanero
Valor en aduanaBase de arancel e IVARevisión de valor, determinación con recargos
Régimen aduaneroObligaciones posterioresTemporal vencida convertida en omisión

Definiciones

  • Incrementables: Los incrementables son los conceptos que se suman al precio pagado para determinar el valor en aduana, como el flete y el seguro hasta el punto de entrada.
  • Rectificación: La rectificación es la corrección formal de un pedimento ya presentado, y es más simple y barata cuanto antes se realice.

Preguntas frecuentes

¿Quién me entrega el pedimento?

Su agente aduanal, como parte del despacho. Consérvelo: es el documento que la autoridad solicitará en cualquier revisión posterior a la operación.

¿El valor en aduana es el precio de mi factura?

No necesariamente. Parte del precio pagado e incorpora incrementables como flete y seguro hasta el punto de entrada, por lo que suele ser mayor que el valor de factura.

¿Sobre qué se calcula el IVA de importación?

Sobre el valor en aduana más el impuesto general de importación y, en su caso, otras contribuciones. El arancel amplía la base del IVA.

¿Puedo corregir un pedimento ya presentado?

Sí, mediante rectificación. Tiene costo y puede implicar demora, pero es considerablemente más barato que esperar a que la autoridad detecte la diferencia.
